A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PC-Winter paper, with all 17 pages and Appendices A–H available. Full text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical content apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original node-dropping and edge-addition experiments on six graph datasets, plus ablations, parameter analyses, and computational measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains the same original experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices, including performance curves and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical PC-Winter procedure: contribution trees, level and precedence constraints, DFS permutations, sampling, hierarchical truncation, local propagation, and aggregation into node and edge values.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six datasets: Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, Amazon-Photo, Amazon-Computer, and Coauthor-Physics. Node-dropping, edge-addition, and appendix test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments. Node-dropping retains Random, Degree, LOO, and Data Shapley; edge-addition retains Random, Edge-Betweenness, and LOO. Appendix comparisons and ablation variants are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix G retain the same inductive splits, two-layer models, accuracy evaluation, node/edge testing procedures, training settings, convergence criterion, and computation limits.

E4.justification: The constraint ablations, permutation-count and truncation-ratio analyses, mixed/labeled-node analyses, and efficiency analyses are identical in Section 4.4 and Appendices D–F and H.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version adds experimental replication counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the permutation-sampling and convergence documentation is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted curves, rankings, and qualitative findings are unchanged, including the performance results in Figures 3–12 and computational results in Tables 1, 4, and 5.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and constraints in Sections 2–3, the Winter-value formulation in Appendix B, and the specificity and exhaustiveness theorems and proofs in Appendix C are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion make identical claims about graph data valuation, PC-Winter, efficient approximation, and empirical effectiveness. No contribution or novelty claim changes scope.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitations concerning scalability and restriction to homogeneous graphs in Section 5, with the scalability limitation reiterated in Appendix H.4.

D1.justification: Appendix G provides identical dataset statistics, split instructions, convergence details, hyperparameters, and NVIDIA Titan RTX computation-limit information. No implementation or resource-access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the bibliography are identical, preserving the same cited works and positioning relative to Shapley/Winter values, existing data valuation methods, and graph neural networks.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv:2402.01943v1 dated 2 Feb 2024 to arXiv:2402.01943v2 dated 8 Mar 2024. This is an administrative text update; the paper's wording, headings, and organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12, Tables 1–5, captions, axes, legends, placement, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages are identical except for the text of the first-page version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, reproducibility details, and presentation remain identical throughout the main text and appendices. The administrative version/date update provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
